reason: Rich cross-verified documentation across NASA, Scientific American, Halley Space, and historical surveys thoroughly debunks the visibility myth with precise optical arithmetic.
story: For over two centuries, a popular legend claimed the Great Wall of China is the only human structure visible from the Moon. The rumor began in a 1754 letter by antiquarian William Stukeley, centuries before spaceflight existed. But when humans actually reached space, physics destroyed the myth. From the Moon, spotting a ten-meter-wide wall is optically equivalent to spotting a human hair from a kilometer away. Even from the International Space Station, orbiting 400 kilometers up, the wall is roughly ten times narrower than the human eye's resolving limit of one arcminute. Compounding the problem, the wall was built from local stone and dirt, camouflaging it against the surrounding landscape. China's own first astronaut, Yang Liwei, confirmed he could not see it at all. While orbiting cameras with telephoto lenses have captured it, unaided human eyes simply cannot.
angle: At 400 kilometers up on the space station, the Great Wall is roughly ten times narrower than the optical resolving limit of the human eye.

claims.claim: The myth that the Great Wall can be seen from the Moon was recorded in a 1754 letter by English antiquarian William Stukeley.
The Great Wall cannot be seen from the Moon with the naked human eye.
China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, stated after his spaceflight that he was unable to see the Great Wall from space.
The angular resolution limit of the human eye is approximately one arcminute.
The International Space Station orbits at an altitude of approximately 400 kilometers above Earth.
The widest sections of the Great Wall measure roughly 9 to 10 meters across.
From low Earth orbit, the Great Wall is roughly ten times narrower than what the naked human eye can resolve.
The Great Wall blends into surrounding terrain because it was constructed from local materials like stone and dirt.
Astronaut Leroy Chiao photographed sections of the Great Wall from the International Space Station using a telephoto lens.
Astronaut Leroy Chiao admitted he did not see the Great Wall with his naked eye and was initially unsure if his photo showed it.
The Great Wall of China can be identified from space using spaceborne radar imaging.
The Pyramids of Giza in Egypt are visible from the International Space Station.
The Three Gorges Dam in China is over 2.3 kilometers long and visible from the International Space Station.
City lights on Earth at night are easily visible to astronauts in low Earth orbit.
A survey by China's cultural heritage administration determined that all associated Great Wall fortifications span 21,196 kilometers (13,170 miles).
The Ming dynasty portion of the Great Wall measures 8,850 kilometers (5,500 miles) in total length.
The Ming Great Wall consists of 6,259 kilometers of wall sections, 359 kilometers of trenches, and 2,232 kilometers of natural defensive barriers.
Qin Shi Huang linked earlier regional fortifications to defend against northern invaders around 220 to 221 BC.
Sticky rice mortar made with slaked lime was used to bond bricks during construction of the Great Wall.

disputed: Origin of the Moon visibility claim: Source S1 and S4 cite William Stukeley's 1754 letter, whereas S5 attributes the start of the myth to a 1923 National Geographic article, and S4 also highlights Richard Halliburton's 1938 book. A script should attribute: 'According to historical records, the myth dates back to at least a 1754 letter by William Stukeley.'

Human remains in the wall: S1 and S6 state that no human bones or bodies were ever incorporated into the mortar or structure, whereas S5 claims deceased workers were buried in its foundation. A script should note: 'Urban legends claim bodies were built into the wall, but archaeological evidence finds no human bones in the mortar.'

Naked-eye orbital visibility: S1 mentions past astronauts Gene Cernan and Ed Lu claimed to see it under exceptional conditions, but S2, S3, and S4 demonstrate that human eye resolution limits and camouflage make naked-eye detection virtually impossible without magnification. A script should state: 'While a couple of astronauts claimed brief glimpses, optical physics and NASA confirm it cannot be reliably resolved by unaided human vision.'
